## What it is

Nextcloud is a personal cloud: file sync and sharing, calendars, contacts and many add-on apps, used from a browser, the desktop sync client and phone apps ([nextcloud/server](https://github.com/nextcloud/server)).

**Licence:** `AGPL-3.0` (GitHub licence API; `research-output/evidence/license-matrix.csv` row "Nextcloud server"). Market class **L2**. OneMind ships the upstream image unmodified as a separate program.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): files: cloud, sync, calendar-contacts. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) with three containers: `nextcloud` (the official `nextcloud:33.0.10-apache` image), and native sidecars `postgres` (PostgreSQL 18, the version the Nextcloud 33 admin manual recommends) and `valkey` (Redis-compatible, for file locking; `REDIS_HOST`).
- The database runs as a native sidecar in the same pod and listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so no other pod can reach it. For that reason PostgreSQL trusts local connections and there is no database password and no Secret (contract §11.2 forbids committed Secrets; §12.18 `spec.secrets` with generated values is not in the schema yet). When `spec.secrets` exists, a generated password can replace `trust`.
- Nextcloud runs as UID 33 (`www-data`), as the README section "Running as an arbitrary user" describes; PostgreSQL and Valkey run as UID 999. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped. Apache keeps port 80: the pod sets the namespaced sysctl `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0` (in the Kubernetes safe set), which affects only this pod's network namespace.
- PHP `conf.d` is a writable copy: with `REDIS_HOST` set, the image's entrypoint writes `/usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/redis-session.ini` on every start, and as UID 33 it cannot write the image's root-owned directory (the container exits with "Permission denied"). The `php-conf` init container copies the image's `conf.d` into an emptyDir mounted there, on every pod start, so a new image's PHP settings still apply.
- Volumes: `nextcloud-html` (20 GiB, `/var/www/html`: code, config and every user's files) and `nextcloud-db` (5 GiB). Valkey keeps nothing.
- Probes: `GET /status.php` (startup allows 10 minutes for the first code copy), `pg_isready` and `valkey-cli ping` for the sidecars.

## First run

Source: the nextcloud/docker [README](https://github.com/nextcloud/docker#readme) ("Auto configuration via environment variables").

1. Install Nextcloud from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-nextcloud`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:8080:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-nextcloud port-forward svc/nextcloud 8080:80
   ```
3. The installer page shows the PostgreSQL settings already filled in. Choose the admin user name and password and finish the installation. Until then **anyone who can reach the page can create the admin account**, so do this right after install.
4. To use another address later (a LAN name or the app proxy), add it to `trusted_domains` with `occ config:system:set trusted_domains 1 --value=<host>`, run inside the container as in the README ("Accessing the Nextcloud command-line interface (`occ`)").

## Not done yet

- Background jobs use AJAX (the default); a cron sidecar is not packaged.
- No SMTP and no Collabora or OnlyOffice.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: it has not been tested against this image.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices where upstream gives none; they are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212765046, job `gate (nextcloud)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/library/nextcloud:33.0.10-apache`: CRITICAL CVE-2026-42216 and CVE-2026-42217 in `libopenexr-3-1-30` 3.1.13-2, fixed in 3.2.12-1~deb13u1.
- Vulnerability: `docker.io/library/postgres:18.6-trixie`: CRITICAL CVE-2025-68121 in the Go `stdlib` v1.24.6, fixed in 1.24.13, 1.25.7 or 1.26.0-rc.3.
- Secret finding (Trivy): the nextcloud image has a rule hit `azure-storage-account-key` (CRITICAL) in `/usr/src/nextcloud/3rdparty/microsoft/azure-storage-common/src/Common/Internal/Resources.php`; the postgres image has `private-key` (HIGH) in `/etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key` (Debian's ssl-cert package). Both are in upstream images we do not build. The gate counts any finding as a failure and is not relaxed.
- Passed: licence AGPL-3.0, ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.
